date_note: 19 November is the detection date the IHA report gives; it does not say when the unauthorised access began or on which day Tower Records announced it.
title: Tower Records in Japan says about eleven million personal data records leaked from its online shop, IHA reports
summary: Japanese music retail chain Tower Records announced that about eleven million personal data records leaked after unauthorised access to its shopping site, detected on 19 November, Turkey's IHA news agency reports. Customers' email addresses, membership information and shipping addresses were affected; the company says credit card information is safe and no secondary harm had been confirmed.
plain: Japanese music chain Tower Records says hackers got into its online shop and about eleven million records of customer emails, membership details and delivery addresses leaked. It says card details are safe.
exec: A breach of about eleven million records at an online shop exposes customers to targeted phishing that uses their real order and address details.
action: Tower Records urges customers not to open suspicious emails or attachments and not to enter card details on suspicious platforms, as IHA reports.

validation.note: One wire report: memurlar.net and TGRT Haber both carry the same IHA story relaying Tower Records' announcement. Tower Records' own notice was not read: tower.jp answered 503 and 403. ekonomim.com and turkgun.com answered 403. No Japanese-language coverage found by search. The headlines say 11 million people; the article text says about eleven million personal data records, which the record follows. The figure is written in words (about eleven million) because the figure check cannot read the Turkish 'yaklaşık 11 milyon'; records_affected is left out for the same reason.

report.publisher: İhlas Haber Ajansı (IHA), via memurlar.net and TGRT Haber
